name: Harrowmere Hall
blurb: A storm cuts a fenland country house off from the world on Friday night. By Saturday morning the host is dead and everyone under the roof has something to hide.
contentNotes: Golden-age mystery tone. One off-screen death; no gore, no explicit content. Fictional people, places and events only.

realism.rationale: Grounded tracks pocket money, keys and the evidence you carry, with simple routines for the household, without the bookkeeping of a full simulation.

currency.label: Pounds, shillings and pence
currency.note: Pre-decimal money. A pint of bitter is 4d, a village-inn room 7s 6d, a gardener's wage about 35s a week.

start.summary: You have just stepped out of the motor-taxi at Harrowmere Hall with your valuer's case, a bank book and an invitation to dinner. The sky over the fens is the colour of slate.

places.name: Harrowmere Estate
places.description: A low, wet estate of reed beds, drove roads and willows, set on a rise of firmer ground in the fens. The nearest village is Saltreach, two and a half miles away by the causeway.

places.name: The Mere Causeway
places.description: A raised gravel road across the marsh, covered by the mere at the highest tides. In a hard south-westerly it can be impassable for hours.

places.name: Saltreach
places.description: A small fenland village of brick cottages, a church, a public house and a police constable. The only telephone exchange for miles is in the post office.

places.name: The Gatehouse
places.description: A brick lodge at the end of the drive, empty since the old gardener retired. The estate's telephone line comes in here before running to the hall on a line of poles.

places.name: Harrowmere Hall
places.description: A rambling red-brick house with a Jacobean core, Victorian additions and a conservatory that never quite matched either. Wind finds its way into every passage.

places.name: Entrance Hall
places.description: A flagged hall with a grandfather clock, a long oak settle and a staircase that creaks on the fourth step. The butler's pantry opens off it.

places.name: The Library
places.description: Walls of leather spines, a worn Turkey carpet, a tray of decanters and a deep fireplace. The mantel is carved with a date in Roman numerals. A door in the east wall leads to the study.

places.name: Sir Alaric's Study
places.description: A small, orderly room with a roll-top desk, a portrait of Sir Alaric's father and a framed estate map. A typewriter sits under a cover on a side table.

places.name: The Drawing Room
places.description: Chintz sofas, a baby grand nobody plays and a tall window onto the drive. After dinner the household gathers here for coffee.

places.name: The Dining Room
places.description: A long mahogany table under a dim chandelier, with twelve chairs and a sideboard that is polished every morning whether or not anyone eats.

places.name: The Kitchen
places.description: A flagged kitchen with a vast range, copper pans and a scrubbed table where the staff take their meals. A door leads to the yard and another to the cellar steps.

places.name: The Conservatory
places.description: A glass-and-iron room of potted palms and wicker chairs. A garden door opens onto a gravel path to the boathouse.

places.name: The Bedroom Corridor
places.description: A long first-floor corridor with doors to the family and guest bedrooms. Floorboards creak, and a light under a door can be seen from the stairs.

places.name: The Cellar
places.description: A cool vaulted cellar of wine racks, coal and trunks. The house's main fuse board is bolted to the wall by the steps.

places.name: The Boathouse
places.description: A tarred wooden shed on the edge of the mere with a slipway, a stack of nets and a flat-bottomed punt. A damp path through the reeds leads up to the conservatory.

characters.name: The Guest
characters.role: Antiquarian valuer invited to appraise part of the Thorne collection
characters.summary: You were asked to value a handful of pieces before the autumn sale, and you accepted because Sir Alaric's collection is one of the best private ones in the Fens. You notice things for a living.

characters.name: Sir Alaric Thorne
characters.summary: A big, courteous man with a heart condition he refuses to discuss. He collects clocks, maps and quarrels in about equal measure, and has the gift of making every guest feel they are his favourite.

goals.label: Show off the collection and settle family business at breakfast
steps: Receive the valuer and show the clocks
Speak privately with someone after breakfast

characters.name: Lady Honoria Thorne
characters.summary: Composed, quick and fond of crossword puzzles and cold tea. She runs the household in all but name and has long since learned which of her husband's disputes to ignore.

regard.note: Cannot quite give up on him.

goals.label: Hold the household together through the weekend
steps: Keep Rupert and Alaric apart at dinner

characters.name: Captain Rupert Thorne
characters.summary: Charming, restless and always somewhere else in his head. He served with distinction, drinks a little too much, and owes money in more than one town.

schedule.activity: lounging with a magazine and a drink
a conversation he does not mention

characters.name: Verity Lorne
characters.summary: Quiet, exact and easy to overlook, which she uses. She types faster than she speaks and knows where every paper in the house is kept.

regard.note: Afraid of him and not sure why she should be.

characters.name: Julian Ashcombe
characters.summary: Urbane, silver-haired and fond of telling stories at his own expense. He has handled the Thornes' affairs for twenty years and is everyone's idea of a safe pair of hands.

schedule.activity: stepping out for a few minutes

characters.name: Dr. Lionel Farrant
characters.summary: A brisk, kind man with large hands and a habit of patting his pockets. He has treated Sir Alaric's heart for eight years and is more worried about it than he lets on.

schedule.activity: tea and talk, bag set down by the sofa
coffee and a quiet word with Lady Honoria

goals.label: Get Sir Alaric to rest and take his drops on time
steps: Refill the bottle of heart tincture
Speak to Lady Honoria about the strain

characters.name: Gideon Pell
characters.summary: Tall, grave and perfectly silent on the stairs. He has served the Thornes for thirty years and measures his own worth by how little anyone ever notices him.

schedule.activity: opening the house and lighting fires

characters.name: Mrs. Dorothea Marsh
characters.summary: Square, rosy and entirely unflappable. She feeds the household, manages the maids and notices everything that passes through her kitchen. She dislikes gossip and will tell you anything if you are kind to her.

goals.label: Feed everyone through the storm
steps: Check the larder and the coal

characters.name: Nell Sparrow
characters.summary: Quick, nervous and kind. She has worked at the Hall for two years, sees the whole house before anyone else is up, and is terrified of Mr. Pell.

goals.label: Get through the weekend without Mr. Pell noticing her
steps: Finish the fires before half past seven
Keep out of the butler's way
Ask Mrs. Marsh for Sunday afternoon off

characters.name: Constable Albert Hobbs
characters.summary: A solid, patient man on a bicycle, with a notebook and a strong sense of what is and is not his business. He has never had a case bigger than a stolen pig.

goals.label: Keep Saltreach quiet
steps: Check the tide tables each morning
Answer any call from the Hall

truth.label: What happened in the library
truth.truth: Julian Ashcombe, the family's solicitor and a trustee of the Thorne Trust, had taken about eleven thousand four hundred pounds over six years by paying it to a fictitious 'M. Rutherford'. Verity Lorne noticed the pattern while indexing the papers and told Sir Alaric on Thursday. Sir Alaric invited Ashcombe to confront him on Saturday after breakfast and asked the valuer to attend as an independent witness. At about five to eleven on Friday night Ashcombe fetched a clean glass from the kitchen; at five past he joined Sir Alaric in the library for a brandy to 'talk through the papers', and put a lethal dose of digitalis tincture, taken from Dr. Farrant's bag in the drawing room, into his host's glass. Sir Alaric's known heart condition and prescription meant that his death would pass as natural. Ashcombe rinsed his own glass, burned a page of the ledger, left by the conservatory door and went back to bed.

rewards.text: The player learns the whole truth.

lore.title: Harrowmere Hall
lore.text: Harrowmere Hall stands on a rise of firm ground in the fens, built round a Jacobean core and added to by every generation of Thornes. The west wing burned in 1887 and was rebuilt in a brisker brick. The house is damp, draughty and beloved; it is also famous for its collection of clocks and maps.

lore.title: The Thorne family
lore.text: The Thornes have held Harrowmere for three hundred years, and the baronetcy for two. They farmed the fen, drained it, lost money and made it back. The present family is Sir Alaric, Lady Honoria and, as heir, Sir Alaric's nephew Captain Rupert Thorne; the Thornes have no children of their own.

lore.title: The Mere Causeway
lore.text: The causeway is a raised gravel road of about two miles that connects the estate to Saltreach. At the highest tides, or when a gale pushes the mere up, it can be impassable for a day. Estate people know the tide tables by heart; visitors are told to check before they set out.

lore.title: Saltreach
lore.text: Saltreach is a village of about two hundred, with a church, a public house called the Heron, a post office with the district's telephone exchange and one police constable. The Thornes have been its principal family for as long as anyone remembers.

lore.title: The Thorne collection
lore.text: Sir Alaric's collection of English clocks and fen maps is one of the finest private ones in eastern England. This autumn he has decided to sell a selection at auction to fund repairs to the Hall, and he has invited a London valuer to appraise the pieces before the sale.

lore.title: Sir Alaric Thorne
lore.text: Sir Alaric Thorne is sixty-two, big, courteous and given to long stories about clocks. He has had a weak heart for eight years and takes drops from Dr. Farrant as directed, though he has been known to forget. He likes to host house parties and to settle disputes before breakfast.

lore.title: Lady Honoria Thorne
lore.text: Lady Honoria is Sir Alaric's wife of thirty-three years. She runs the house calmly and dryly, solves the newspaper's crossword every day and has never been known to raise her voice.

lore.title: Captain Rupert Thorne
lore.text: Captain Rupert Thorne is Sir Alaric's nephew and heir. Charming, restless and a little vague about money, he is said in Saltreach to owe more than he earns. His uncle has bailed him out twice and has said that he will not do so a third time.

lore.title: Verity Lorne
lore.text: Miss Verity Lorne has been Sir Alaric's secretary for four years. She is quiet, exact and loyal, and has never been late with a letter. The household calls her 'the filing cabinet' and relies on her to find anything.

lore.title: Julian Ashcombe
lore.text: Julian Ashcombe is the Thorne family's solicitor and a trustee of the family trust. He has handled their affairs for twenty years and is respected across the county. A frequent weekend guest, he is as much a part of the furniture as the grandfather clock.

lore.title: Dr. Lionel Farrant
lore.text: Dr. Farrant has been the family's physician for fifteen years, Sir Alaric's heart specialist for eight, and a friend for longer. He carries his black bag everywhere and puts it down wherever he stops.

lore.title: Gideon Pell
lore.text: Pell has been the Hall's butler for thirty years. He is tall, grave and impeccably discreet, and he holds the keys to the cellar, the plate cupboard and most of the household's secrets. He is also the one person who can say how the house is meant to run.

lore.title: Mrs. Dorothea Marsh
lore.text: Mrs. Marsh has cooked at the Hall for twenty years. She is solid, kind and unshockable, and her kitchen is the warmest room in the house. She dislikes gossip but will tell a friend a great deal.

lore.title: Nell Sparrow
lore.text: Nell Sparrow is nineteen, the Hall's youngest servant, and the first person up each morning. She lights the fires, dusts the library and is afraid of Mr. Pell. She sees the house before anyone else has made a mess of it.

lore.title: Constable Albert Hobbs
lore.text: Constable Hobbs has kept the peace in Saltreach for eleven years, mostly by bicycle. He is patient, thorough and slow to hurry, and has never had a case bigger than a stolen pig. He gets to the Hall as fast as the tide lets him.

lore.title: The Library
lore.text: The library is the heart of the house. It has leather-bound sets of the county histories, a worn Turkey carpet and a fireplace carved with the year the west wing was rebuilt. Guests are encouraged to take a book; Sir Alaric prefers that they put it back.

lore.title: Sir Alaric's study
lore.text: The study is Sir Alaric's private office. It holds a roll-top desk, the estate map and a wall safe behind the portrait of his father. It is generally known that he keeps important papers in the safe.

lore.title: The Conservatory
lore.text: The conservatory was added in 1902 and has never been warm. A garden door leads to a path through the reeds to the boathouse; the family use it in summer and the staff use it for shortcuts.

lore.title: The telephone
lore.text: The house has one telephone, in the entrance hall, connected to the Saltreach exchange by a line on wooden poles. The line has failed in gales before. The estate keeps a tool roll in the gatehouse for just such repairs.

lore.title: The lantern on the mere
lore.text: Estate children claim that a lantern walks on the mere on stormy nights and that it belongs to the first Thorne, who drowned crossing the causeway. Mrs. Marsh says it is marsh gas. Nell has never been out to look.

lore.title: Dinner at Harrowmere
lore.text: Dinner at Harrowmere is at half past seven, and everyone dresses. Sir Alaric presides, Lady Honoria sits at the other end, and conversation is expected to be general and sometimes loud. Coffee is taken in the drawing room.

args.text: The earpiece hisses and clicks. The line is dead.
The exchange puts you through to Saltreach. The constable says he will come as soon as the causeway allows.
With pliers, tape and a length of copper wire from the tool roll you rejoin the severed line. The earpiece hums again.

args.text: Dr. Farrant admits, reluctantly, that Sir Alaric's death looks nothing like a heart simply failing.
